\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Hermite coefficients of multilinear polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_multilinear}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_multilinear}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_finset_sum_hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_indicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.indicatorMultiIndex_eq_iff, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ assign a real coefficient $F(S)$ to each subset
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$. The Hermite coefficient at
$\alpha$ of the polynomial $x\mapsto\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}F(S)\prod_{i\in
S}x_i$ is $F(\{i:\alpha_i=1\})$ if every $\alpha_i\le 1$, and is $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}
